$comment: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for iOS colour tokens.
Mirrored into: (a) the Figma file 'Passkey Vault — iOS Design System' collection 'PV Color',
NOTHING auto-syncs Figma -> .xcassets. This file is the join. Edit here, then re-run the generator.
Every light value was derived in OKLCH (hue and chroma preserved, lightness reduced) until it
reached WCAG AA 4.5:1 against surface/default light (#FFFFFF). The raw web palette in
docs/UI-DESIGN.md is tuned for dark surfaces and fails AA on light ones — teal at 2.02:1 and
amber at 1.66:1 are the extremes. Do not 'restore' the web values here without re-checking contrast.

tokens.note: Page background. Unchanged from the existing catalog.
Cards, list cells, sheets. Unchanged.
NEW. Middle elevation step for grouped-list section backgrounds. Dark is the base-200 #212121 the catalog was missing entirely — it jumped #1F1F1F straight to #262626.
Body text. Unchanged.
Secondary text. Unchanged; already AA in both modes.

CHANGED. Was #E16540 in both appearances, which measured 3.42:1 on white as text and 3.42:1 under a white button label — both below AA. Light is brand coral darkened in OKLCH; dark is it lightened, because #E16540 was only 4.42:1 on #262626. This one value serves as text on surface AND as a primary button fill under white.

NEW. The label colour used ON a PVAccent fill. UI-DESIGN.md defines this as 'Primary content #FFFFFF' with a single value — that is incomplete for iOS, because the two roles of the accent pull in opposite directions in dark mode. PVAccent dark had to be LIGHTENED (#E36742) so it passes as text on a dark surface, which necessarily makes a white label on it worse: white measures 3.34:1 there and fails. A dark label measures 4.93:1 and passes. So light mode knocks out in white, dark mode knocks out in near-black. Discovered by whiteLabelOnAccentFillMeetsWcagAaInBothAppearances failing against a hardcoded white.

NEW. The literal brand coral from UI-DESIGN.md, preserved for LARGE TEXT (>=18pt regular / >=14pt bold) and decorative fills only. 3.42:1 on white — deliberately exempt from the AA text gate, and must never be bound to small text.
NEW. Passkey / passwordless — semantically the most brand-load-bearing token in the product, and it did not exist on iOS at all. Web teal #00CDB7 is 2.02:1 on white.
NEW. Strong password, no breach detected.
NEW. Old or reused password. Web amber #FFBE00 is 1.66:1 on white — the worst offender in the palette.
Unchanged. The light value was already hand-picked in this catalog at 4.80:1; kept over the derived #DC3545 because it is slightly more conservative. This is the precedent the whole approach follows.
NEW. Neutral notices.
NEW. Links and info accents (UI-DESIGN.md calls this 'secondary').

NEW (38-06). The favicon icon tile's ground -- deliberately the SAME value in both appearances, mirroring web's --pv-tile-bg. GitHub's favicon is black and vanishes on a dark tile (found in live review, packages/pv-ui/components/ItemIconTile.tsx's own comment); this token exists precisely so the favicon tile never follows PVSurfaceAlt into dark mode's #212121. Not a text-bearing surface, so no contrast_min.

NEW (38-06). Literal third-party brand mark colour, transcribed from packages/pv-ui/components/ItemIconTile.tsx's CardBrandTile -- not part of the PV semantic palette, exempt from the design system's own AA gate the way a logo mark is. Fixed in both appearances (web does not flip Visa's tile either).

NEW (38-06). Same provenance as PVCardBrandVisa. Web additionally flips this tile's background to a light neutral in its dark theme (Tailwind `[[data-theme=vault-dark]_&]:bg-zinc-100`); iOS keeps the single light-theme value in both appearances for now -- a recorded, deliberate visual-parity simplification, not a security or functional gap (38-06-SUMMARY.md).
NEW (38-06). Same provenance as PVCardBrandVisa.
NEW (38-06). Same provenance as PVCardBrandMastercard -- web flips this one's background to zinc-100 in dark theme too; iOS keeps the single light-theme value (same recorded simplification).

NEW (38-06). The wordmark colour ON the four card-brand tiles above -- fixed white in both appearances because the tiles themselves are fixed brand colours that do not follow the system appearance (unlike PVOnAccent, which deliberately DOES flip because PVAccent itself flips). Exists so `scripts/audit-ios-colour-tokens.sh` check 1's blanket `.white` prohibition has a real token to point at instead of a literal.
